hosting.$comment_ignore: The dotfile glob is spelled out rather than '**/.*': the Claude Code plugin (§R3) keeps its manifest in /lib/claude-plugin/.claude-plugin/, and a blanket '**/.*' would silently drop it from the deploy. frontend/build is generated, so the only dot-entries that can appear there are the ones listed here.
hosting.$comment_headers: The hosted SDK, /lib/** (docs/plan/agents.html §M). Hosting applies EVERY matching block, later ones winning a header the earlier ones also set — so the wide rules come first and the specific ones last. scripts/deploy-lib.mjs stages the files; scripts/deploy-lib-check.mjs asserts these headers against a running hosting emulator.

headers.comment: Anything under /lib is meant to be fetched cross-origin: a browser <script type=module>, a Deno URL import, an npm tarball URL.
Content types hosting would otherwise guess wrong: .ts is NOT video/mp2t here, and a .tgz served as octet-stream makes npm's download path fussy. .d.ts ends in .ts, so one rule covers both.
The Claude plugin (§R3) is served as a browsable folder as well as a zip: hosting guesses nothing useful for .md, and a plugin bundle downloaded as octet-stream confuses the browser's Save dialog.
Pinned: the files under /lib/v1 are what a consumer's lockfile and an editor's cache point at, so they are immutable for a year.
The moving name: always the newest build, so nothing may keep a copy.

The install page changes with the docs; revalidate it every time. A header rule is matched against the REQUEST PATH, not the file hosting resolves it to, and a trailing slash is normalised away — so /lib/ needs the '/lib' spelling and only a direct hit needs '/lib/index.html'.
The plugin moves with every release and carries the whole integration context inside it, so a cached copy is a copy that describes an older API. Revalidate, never store.

A URL import only carries types if the server says where they are. Deno reads this header (and the triple-slash reference the bundle starts with); an absolute path so it resolves the same from any importing module. sdk*.js is sdk.js and sdk.min.js.

THE ARTIFACT DRIVER, /backend-driver/** (docs/plan/artifacts.html §E1) — the same arrangement as /lib/**, for the same reasons. An artifact loads driver.js from ANOTHER origin (the usercontent site, inside a sandbox whose origin is 'null'), and a Vite or TypeScript project imports driver.mjs and its .d.ts by URL: so CORS is open and nosniff makes the types below the final word.
.ts is not video/mp2t here; .d.ts ends in .ts, so one rule covers both.
A module script is refused under nosniff unless it is served as JavaScript, and hosting does not know .mjs.
Pinned: what a published artifact's <script src> points at. Immutable for a year — a fix ships as a new file under the same major only if it cannot break an artifact that is already out there.
The moving name: revalidated every time.
A URL import only carries types if the server says where they are (as /lib/v1/sdk*.js does).

The integration context an orchestrator is pointed at (docs/plan/agents.html §O). Generated by scripts/gen-integration.mjs; scripts/deploy-lib-check.mjs asserts these headers against a running hosting emulator. An agent fetches these from anywhere, so CORS is open, and they are NEVER cached: an agent that re-reads the page is asking whether its knowledge is current, and a cached answer would defeat the question. The charset is explicit so a fetch cannot guess latin-1 on the em dashes.
The readable page. Three spellings because a header rule matches the REQUEST path: what people type, the normalised directory, and the file itself.
The Claude setup guide (§R3) — the same three spellings, for the same reason.

THE PWA (docs/plan/agents.html §S). None of these carry a content hash, so hosting's default hour of caching would decide how long a phone keeps the old app: a service worker that is not revalidated is a deploy nobody receives. 'no-cache' means revalidate, not 'do not store' — a 304 is still cheap. Service-Worker-Allowed is belt and braces for the '/' scope.
Hosting would otherwise guess .webmanifest wrong; a browser that does not see a manifest type will not offer to install.

hosting.$comment_target: Two Hosting sites (docs/plan/artifacts.html §D1). 'app' is the SPA and every door; 'usercontent' serves artifact files and nothing else. The targets are named in .firebaserc for the emulator project; scripts/deploy-functions.mjs writes the real site ids into firebase.deploy.json ({project} and {project}-usercontent). The app site stays FIRST: tools that read 'the hosting config' (scripts/deploy-lib-check.mjs, the e2e header checks) take the first entry.
hosting.$comment_rewrites: The SPA fallback is everything EXCEPT /c/**: artifact files are served only on the usercontent site, so on the app's own origin that path is a plain 404 rather than the app shell answering 200 for a file that is not there.

hosting.$comment: THE USERCONTENT SITE (docs/plan/artifacts.html §D1): somebody else's code, served from an origin that is not the app's. Its ONLY route is /c/** → the api function (backend/src/doors/artifactContent.ts), which verifies the capability in the path and streams the file. Nothing of the app is here — no index.html, no service worker, no /api — so everything else is the 404 page in backend/usercontent. The function sets the sandbox CSP itself on every /c response; the header block below covers what hosting answers on its own (the 404).

headers.value: sandbox allow-scripts allow-forms allow-popups allow-downloads allow-modals
